summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator, Checker and Rio discuss how to disrupt Pithica's far-flung network of revenue streams. The narrator proposed mass tip-offs warning victims their money was being stolen, but Checker argued that no one would take such messages seriously because the sources are diverse and the messages would be dismissed or filtered as spam. Checker suggested a Trojan to alter the accounts, but the narrator noted people would not check them quickly enough. The narrator then decides to seek help from a shadowy multinational organization that can pull every string, despite its earlier threat to kill them, and asks Rio for a disposable phone.
one_line: The narrator and Checker debate how to expose Pithica's revenue streams, and the narrator resolves to contact a dangerous shadowy organization for help.
key_facts: The narrator had planned to send massive tip-offs warning people that their money was being stolen or not going where they believed.
Checker argued that the tip-offs would not be taken seriously because Pithica's network comes from all over the world.
The narrator said a mass communication would be dismissed in less than zero time and probably would not get past most people's spam filters.
Checker proposed sending a Trojan that would alter all of the accounts so that people would see something happening when they were checked.
The narrator replied that nobody would check the accounts even if told to, and that people needed to move their money simultaneously.
The narrator said Pithica knows the group is out there and has the information, so it is only a matter of time before Pithica tracks them down or changes its revenue structure.
The narrator proposed asking a shadowy multinational organization that can pull every string in the book for the authority they need.
Checker said that the shadowy organization had already said it would kill them.
The narrator responded, "Then they can't do much worse, can they?"
Checker said the narrator was going to get her own way on this despite his objections.
Rio opened a kitchen drawer containing a jumble of disposable cell phones still in their packaging.
Rio handed the narrator a disposable phone, which she intended to burn after use.
Rio asked whether the narrator thought the plan was viable, and she replied, "It's what we've got."

entities.name: Pithica
entities.role: entity whose thousands of revenue streams the group is trying to expose and disrupt

entities.name: Checker
entities.role: companion who works with computers and objects to the plan to contact the shadowy organization

entities.name: Rio
entities.role: companion in the kitchen who supplies the disposable cell phone

entities.name: shadowy multinational organization
entities.role: organization that can pull every string in the book and had previously threatened to kill the group
